To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the OLAE ICP is an efficient and robust algorithm for aligning point clouds and that the OLAE is the optimal method for attitude estimation from vector measurements, with the additional benefit of being the fastest among all known methods.

the optimal alignment algorithm can be used as the core of ICP algorithms and that the OLAE algorithm is a robust, accurate and fast method for solving the point cloud registration problem and the attitude estimation from vector data problem.

the OLAE algorithm is a simple, efficient, and accurate solution to the problem of point cloud registration that can be used in a variety of applications, including the alignment of 3D point clouds and the estimation of the attitude of a rigid body.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following contributions: (1) We introduce a new method to solve the optimal alignment problem of a set of points, lines or planes.
the development and analysis of algorithms for solving the problems of point cloud alignment and attitude estimation from noisy vector observations.
the problem of finding an efficient, accurate, and robust method to estimate the SE(3)-transformation that minimizes a given cost function from a set of geometric features.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal linear method is the fastest one, and it is the best choice when no initial guess is available.
the optimal linear solution is the best option for most applications, and that the non linear Gauss Newton solution is only needed for very specific cases where the linear solution fails.
the proposed method provides a robust and fast alignment of point clouds with the optimal linear solution of Wahba's problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the first time, the optimal linear attitude estimation method is used to perform robust registration of geometric features.

we present a simple approach to integrate geometric features into a single cost function, we compare the performance of several solutions for attitude estimation, we propose a robust loss function, we show how to overcome the singularity of the Gibbs vector, and we present experiments that validate the suitability of our approach for the core of an ICP algorithm.

we have developed a simple and robust algorithm for the registration of geometric features, that is based on the OLAE method, and that can be used to solve the ICP problem in the context of 3D point cloud processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the OLAE algorithm can be used to solve the problem of point to point, point to line, line to point, point cloud registration, and attitude estimation from multiple vector observations in a robust and efficient manner.
the use of the OLAE for solving point cloud registration problems is robust and fast and that it is a good candidate to become the core of an ICP/OLAE algorithm.
a single, fast and robust algorithm can be used to solve both point cloud registration and Wahba's problem with a wide variety of geometric features.
